Verify-Command: python -m pip install -q -e . pytest numpy pandas "wcwidth>=0.6.0" && python -m pytest -q
Allowed-Files: tabulate/cli.py, test/test_cli.py, README.md
Required-Changed-Files: tabulate/cli.py, test/test_cli.py, README.md

## Goal

Extend the `tabulate` command-line utility with validated numeric, text, and
per-column alignment options while preserving its existing defaults and output.
Register `-C` as the short form of `--colalign`, forward all three alignment
settings through every input-file rendering path, and keep the CLI help text
and README usage block synchronized.

## Plan

### Files to touch

- `tabulate/cli.py`: register and parse `-C`, `--colalign`, `--numalign`, and
  `--stralign`; validate their values; forward alignment settings to
  `tabulate()`; and update `_main`'s help docstring.
- `test/test_cli.py`: add in-process exact-output and exact-error coverage for
  the new options and their combinations.
- `README.md`: mirror the updated FORMAT section of the CLI usage block.

### Steps

1. Add the seven specified alignment-help lines to `_main`'s FORMAT section,
   immediately after the integer-format option and before `-f FMT, --format
   FMT`, preserving the indentation and wording that `textwrap.dedent`
   exposes through `--help`.
2. Register `C:` in the short-option specification and add `numalign=` and
   `stralign=` to the long-option specification, retaining the existing
   `colalign=` registration. Initialize numeric and text alignment state to
   the library defaults (`decimal` and `left`) so invocations without these
   options remain unchanged.
3. In the option-reading loop, handle `-C` and `--colalign` together by
   splitting only on whitespace and validating items in left-to-right order.
   Validate `--numalign` against `right`, `center`, `left`, and `decimal`, and
   validate `--stralign` against `right`, `center`, and `left`. On the first
   unsupported value, print `<value> is not a supported alignment` to stderr,
   print the dedented usage text to stdout, and exit with status 3, matching
   the existing unsupported-format behavior. Do not accept `global` or other
   separators.
4. Add `numalign` and `stralign` parameters to the CLI's rendering call chain
   (`_main` to `_open_and_pprint_file` to `_pprint_file`) and pass them as
   keywords to `tabulate()` for every input file, while retaining the current
   `colalign` list behavior and all other option semantics.
5. Add in-process tests using the existing `run_main_in_process` helper for
   the exact default output, `--numalign left`, `--stralign right`, both
   `--colalign` and `-C` aliases, and the combined alignment-plus-grid case.
   Capture stderr for invalid-option cases and assert status 3, the exact
   offending-value message (including the first bad item in a colalign list),
   the complete usage output, and the absence of table output. Cover invalid
   numeric, invalid text (`decimal`), long-form colalign, and short-form
   colalign values, while keeping the existing valid multi-item colalign test.
6. Copy the same seven alignment-help lines into the README usage block in the
   same position, then run `python -m pytest`, `ruff check`, and `ruff format
   --check` to verify the help text remains synchronized and unrelated CLI
   behavior is unchanged.

### Tests to add

- Assert the no-option stdin rendering remains exactly the four lines specified
  by the acceptance criteria.
- Assert exact output for `--numalign left` and `--stralign right`.
- Assert identical exact output for `--colalign "right left"` and the `-C`
  alias with the same argument.
- Assert `--numalign center --stralign center -f grid` produces the exact
  centered grid output.
- For invalid `--numalign`, invalid `--stralign`, invalid long-form
  `--colalign`, and invalid short-form `-C`, assert the exact stderr message,
  usage stdout, status 3, and no rendered table.

## Out of scope

- Changes to `tabulate/__init__.py` or the library API.
- Header alignment, global column alignment, row alignment, or `global` in the
  CLI's colalign values.
- Any change to parsing, defaults, diagnostics, or exit statuses of unrelated
  options.
- A `CHANGELOG` entry, generated `_version.py`, new output formats, or changes
  outside the three listed files.
